Hi Claire — great to hear from you and congrats on the CloudNova sponsorship. Short answers up front: yes, we have multiple ways to attribute partner-sourced credits, but the mechanism affects how the credits are issued and what we need on the legal/finance side.

High level options we commonly use:
- Marketplace entitlement (AWS/Azure/GCP): Sponsor purchases/reserves credits on the marketplace and credits are applied via marketplace entitlements tied to the customer account. This shows up on marketplace billing and partner reporting.
- Partner-managed voucher: Redwood issues promo codes/vouchers that we can mark as "sponsored by CloudNova" in our internal reporting; credits are redeemed through the Redwood Console.
- Hybrid: a marketplace grant coupled with Redwood-side labeling for dashboards & ticketing.

Could you confirm which of the above CloudNova prefers? Also: what legal name should appear on any PO or invoice, and do they require us to issue a formal invoice vs. in-console credit?

If it's helpful, Kimberly and Ben are cc'd and can chime in on finance/process requirements. I can also schedule 20 minutes tomorrow afternoon to align.

— Hannah

Hannah —

Thanks for the ping. Quick finance notes (so Claire and LaunchPad know what's required):
- If CloudNova wants marketplace entitlements: we need confirmation from CloudNova that they will execute the purchase on the marketplace and the target customer account(s) (we need marketplace account IDs). Marketplace entitlements are the cleanest for third-party attribution but are dependent on the partner's marketplace contract.
- If they want Redwood-issued partner vouchers: we require a signed sponsor agreement (we have that attached), plus either a PO from LaunchPad or a sponsor-side invoice request. For accounting we need: sponsor legal name, tax ID (if available), country, and a contact for billing.
- For any method where we apply credits on behalf of a third party, Compliance will want a short statement of purpose in the sponsor agreement and confirmation that no PII will be shared via the credits.

Operationally we handle voucher issuance as a two-step: 1) legal/finance sign-off; 2) fulfillment via Redwood Console. Fulfillment generates a redemption email and a tag that we can mark as "credited_by: CloudNova" for reporting.

I'll attach our internal playbook for partner credits (redwood_credit_instructions.md) to this thread — it lists exact fields we need and SLA for issuance (typically 3–5 business days after paperwork).

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Revenue Operations (Redwood Inference)
